feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV with a clear senior digital communications profile and solid career progression within one organization. It reads professionally and is well targeted, but impact would improve with tighter formatting, fewer repeated ideas, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital strategy/communications brand.  
- Strong credibility: progression from coordinator to director to consultant shows advancement, trust, and depth in one domain.  
- Good use of specifics: Drupal migration, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, analytics stack, and studio build add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidate to save space and sharpen focus.  
- Add more measurable results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include performance gains, engagement lifts, efficiency improvements, budget scope, or team size where possible.  
- Fix writing/style inconsistencies: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lists); standardize punctuation in bullets; “French (A2/Learning)” is awkward—use “French (A2, learning)”; “Topline” may be better as “Key Skills.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with sharper positioning, cleaner phrasing, and 1–2 concrete signals of scale or sector relevance.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Lead with your senior value proposition and sector fit: digital strategy leader for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Tighten the list of channels to avoid sounding inventory-like; emphasize outcomes such as modernization, governance, and audience clarity.
- Consider a rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, and editorial workflows that improve coordination, governance, and audience engagement. Brings deep experience in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination also reappear in Topline Skills and work experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level strengths will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, leadership-level language: “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership”; “Web & CMS administration” → “Web platform management.”
- Reduce overlap with technical sections by focusing on strategic capabilities, e.g.: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform governance • Editorial workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Systems and process improvement • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production
- Standardize style: use parallel noun phrases throughout and avoid mixing broad functions with tactical tasks.
- Consider “cross-functional” instead of “cross-department” for a more modern, concise tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, multi-channel communications, analytics, and advocacy messaging.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with both “Editorial workflow design” and Technical + IT/automation content.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a broad responsibility list. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or named deliverables to distinguish it from the prior NACo leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping duties into impact-led bullets, e.g. “Designed cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia communications.”
- Make deliverables concrete: name the microsite/campaigns, toolkit types, search prototype, or number of properties/templates/modules launched.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: faster publishing, reduced support tickets, improved engagement, search success, adoption by teams, or scale of sites/users supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” overlaps heavily with the Director of Digital Media entry; frame this role as advisory/consulting execution on new initiatives.
- Microsite and AI-search language duplicates Recent Projects; keep the CV item higher-level and let Projects hold the specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with an impact-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing, especially for email/social/video/governance: growth %, production volume, cost savings, turnaround time, engagement lift, or reporting adoption.
- Combine infrastructure/governance bullets for concision: “Built analytics and publishing systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; emphasize enterprise leadership and transformation here instead.
- Video-programming language overlaps with older NACo entries; keep this focused on building the in-house studio and scaling capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with sharper action verbs and any measurable growth.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and outcome-based: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and the footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.
- “improved workflows/editorial coordination” also appears in the Director role; avoid repeating governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should sharpen the highest-value leadership signals and use more distinctive phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with tighter, senior-level language tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications
- Editorial governance and cross-functional content operations
- Multi-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Consider dropping “public-sector” or “audience-focused” if space is tight; they add less differentiation than governance/operations.
- Keep wording parallel: noun phrases only, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with both the header summary and Core Competencies; “member-facing messaging strategy” would feel fresher.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent NACo work, but it’s too broad and duplicates the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize current strengths over listing every tool.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool dump to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Remove “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” from this topline item unless the target role is hands-on technical; it reads lower-level here and is already covered elsewhere.
- Put Drupal first and group the other platforms in parentheses to reflect recency and depth from the 2022–present roles.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large-scale web platform modernization” to align with the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT”; keep topline skills strategic and leave detailed tools to that section.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating both if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with stronger evidence already shown in recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value capabilities and align wording with demonstrated impact.

- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Broadcast video production,” “Livestream and webcast delivery,” “PTZ/multi-camera direction,” “Studio build-out and operations,” “Hybrid event production.”

items.title: University of Virginia

Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and currently overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” and “Core Competencies.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize platform administration strength or differentiated by grouping recent, hands-on CMS experience first.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise, 10,000+ pages) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” if brief context is allowed.
- If keeping as a simple skills line, add proficiency framing in the title: “Web Platforms & CMS Administration” to better match your experience.
- Consider grouping by depth: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint | Power Pages, GitHub Pages” to signal primary vs secondary platforms.
- Keep platform names only; avoid adding modernization/governance language here since that already appears strongly elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” already appears in Topline Skills; consider removing one version or making this section more platform-specific.
- “Web & CMS administration” is already covered in Core Competencies.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools that support your recent Drupal, analytics, and workflow work.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Technical implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and keep naming modern and concise: “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: Front-end: HTML/CSS/JavaScript/jQuery | Integrations: APIs, GTM | Deployment/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add scope or use context elsewhere: e.g., “front-end implementation for Drupal sites,” “tag management and analytics deployment,” or “workflow/deployment automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”). Keep one section broader and this one more tool-specific.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills also overlaps with GitHub Actions; avoid repeating the same capability in both places.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow architecture strength. Since the CV already emphasizes systems-building in recent NACo roles, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated from broader “Workflow automation” references elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/impact: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a raw list, e.g.: **Workflow automation (Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier) • Project/work management (Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp) • Team collaboration (Slack, Microsoft Teams)**
- If space allows, reflect level of use: **Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier; coordinated cross-team delivery in Jira and Asana**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common tools; keep them only if they support a systems/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and avoid restating generic email experience.

Suggested edit
- Rename for precision: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign setup, segmentation, automation, newsletter operations)**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: **enterprise newsletter distribution**, **member communications**, or **journey-based campaigns**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was minimal or dated, remove it rather than padding the list

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with repeated email/newsletter leadership in Work Experience; don’t add phrases like “managed email campaigns” here unless you include a distinct technical angle such as automation, segmentation, or platform administration
- “Engagement” is vague unless supported by member/community tools like Higher Logic; otherwise consider “Email Platforms”

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if known: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience growth, email volume, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the close to show supervision and ownership: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a full version: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and improve multi-channel publishing workflows across web, email, social and video.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this at a lighter, foundational level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work at NACo. It should be tightened and framed around distinctive firsts and cross-functional support, since later roles already cover broader digital leadership.

Suggested edit
- Emphasize the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Tighten the first sentence to show scope and audience value: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy communications.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer outputs: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support program outreach and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/digital production language already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate web/email/social responsibilities here; those are better established in the 2015–2024 positions.
